mission: SSI describes itself as 'the world's first straight-shot SSI lab, with one goal and one product: a safe superintelligence.' It says it approaches 'safety and capabilities in tandem' and plans 'to advance capabilities as fast as possible while making sure our safety always remains ahead,' insulated from short-term commercial pressure. It has published no model, paper or product as of Oct 2026.

key_work.title: SSI founding statement (homepage)
key_work.plain_summary: The company's only substantive public document: building safe superintelligence is 'the most important technical problem of our time', and SSI will do nothing else.

key_work.title: Leadership update: Sutskever becomes CEO
key_work.plain_summary: Co-founder Daniel Gross left on 29 June 2025; Ilya Sutskever became CEO and Daniel Levy President. SSI said it was not looking to be acquired.

key_work.title: NVIDIA long-term strategic partnership
key_work.plain_summary: NVIDIA invested and will supply Vera Rubin systems, expanding SSI's compute about tenfold; the release says SSI has been 'quietly advancing a new research direction to unlock a powerful and robustly aligned artificial intelligence.'

funding_note: Raised $1B (Sep 2024; NFDG, a16z, Sequoia, DST Global, SV Angel per SSI); later rounds reportedly valued it at ~$30–32B; NVIDIA investment Jul 2026 reported by Bloomberg as $5B.
size_note: Small team; press estimates range ~20–50 staff (unconfirmed).

warnings.text: Building safe superintelligence is 'the most important technical problem of our time' (SSI homepage).
Commercial pressures and product cycles can distract from safety; SSI's model is designed to be insulated from them (homepage).

recommendations.text: Treat safety and capabilities as technical problems to be solved together, keeping safety ahead of capabilities (homepage).
Keep a singular focus with no products until safe superintelligence is achieved (homepage).
